Summary In 2025, flood-related losses in Selangor escalated to RM52.9 million from RM22.6 million the prior year, with damages including RM15.3 million to residences, RM4 million to vehicles, and RM1 million to business premises, as reported by the Selangor State Flood Loss Value Statistics.
 Nationwide, Malaysia's flood losses decreased to RM636.9 million from RM933.4 million in 2024, with Terengganu experiencing the most substantial losses.
 The Selangor government is committed to enhancing aid delivery for recurring flood victims and is set to coordinate with the State Disaster Management Unit for this purpose.

 Subscribe SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — Flood losses in Selangor rose to RM52.9 million in 2025 from RM22.6 million the previous year, said Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi.
 Citing the Selangor State Flood Loss Value Statistics for 2024 and 2025 compiled by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) Selangor, he said the losses comprised RM15.3 million in damage to residences, RM4 million to vehicles and RM1 million to business premises.
 Mohd Najwan said agricultural losses and infrastructure damage stood at RM9.6 million and RM26.6 million, respectively.
 “Based on the Special Report on the Impact of Floods in Malaysia 2025 published by DOSM, total flood losses nationwide in 2025 amounted to RM636.9 million, compared with RM933.4 million in 2024.
 “All states in Malaysia were affected by floods, with Terengganu recording the highest losses at RM89.2 million.
 “This was followed by Kelantan and Johor, which recorded losses of RM88.5 million and RM72.1 million, respectively,” he said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
 He was responding to Danial Al-Rashid Haron Aminar Rashid (PH-Batu Tiga), who asked for the estimated annual economic losses arising from incidents such as floods, fires and others.
 Najwan said the state government is committed to improving the quality of aid delivery, particularly in addressing the issue of recurring flood victims, and that the matter would be discussed with the State Disaster Management Unit. — Bernama
